newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Taleban say repulse attack in northwest Afghanistan.
newsitem.headline: Taleban say repulse attack in northwest Afghanistan.

text.p: Afghanistan's purist Islamic Taleban repulsed an attack on their positions in the remote northwestern provinces and inflicted "huge losses", a senior Taleban official said on Wednesday.
Information Minister Amir Khan Mutaqi said forces loyal to the anti-Taleban alliance leader General Abdul Rashid Dostum launched the attack in the provinces of Badghis and Faryab on Tuesday morning.

"Yesterday morning Dostum's forces launched an offensive on the Badghis and Faryab borders. It was repulsed and they suffered huge human and material losses. The fighting continued until midday." Mutaqi told reporters in Kabul.
There was no independent confirmation of Mutaqi's report.

Fierce fighting has raged between the Taleban and the opposition in Badghis and Faryab since Dostum aligned himself in October with forces supporting the ousted government of President Burhanuddin Rabbani.
In a document released on Tuesday, the International Committee of the Red Cross said that since October the fighting had displaced more than 36,000 people towards the Taleban-held city of Herat.
The Taleban control more than 75 per cent of Afghanistan, and have vowed to take the six opposition-held provinces, all in northeastern and central Afghanistan.
Observers in Kabul say that with the Taleban seemingly stalled in the mountains north of the captial, the route through Badghis and Faryab is the most likely point of advance.

"They are going to have a lot of problems trying to get to the north over the mountains, especially in winter. The logical answer would be to try to get in through Badghis where the terrain is more friendly." said one observer, who asked not to be identified.
Mutaqi denied reports carried on the BBC on Tuesday night that the opposition alliance had inflicted heavy casualties on the Taleban forces near the Shibber Pass in central Afghanistan.
"There has been no important fighting in the Shibber Pass, but there have been heavy exchanges of rocket and artillery fire." he said.
The BBC reports quoted an opposition spokesman as saying their forces in the Shibber Pass had repulsed a Taleban offensive and had inflicted more than 100 casualties.
There have been no reports from independent witnesses on recent fighting in the Shibber region.
